sentences.text: Powellvenator is an extinct coelophysoid theropod dinosaur known from fragmentary material, particularly partial hindlimb bones, rather than a complete skeleton.

Martín D. Ezcurra diagnosed the species using distinctive ankle and foot features, including a sigmoid posterodorsal margin on the astragalus, a rounded dorsal expansion on the astragalar body, a calcaneum with a lateral flange, and a strongly reduced metatarsal II shaft.
The specific name podocitus translates to "fast leg".
The generic name Powellvenator honors the late Argentine paleontologist Jaime Eduardo Powell and literally means "Powell's hunter".

Argentine paleontologist José Fernando Bonaparte discovered several unknown dinosaur hindlimbs in the Quebrada de los Jachalleros valley in 1969 and described the skeleton of a small coelophysoid found in the same valley in 1972.
In September 2015, a connection was established between the earliest fossils found and the new taxon discovered in the Los Colorados Formation within the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin.
The only known species, Powellvenator podocitus, was named by Martín D. Ezcurra in 2017 based on partial hindlimb remains from the Los Colorados Formation.
The description of Powellvenator expanded the known record of early neotheropod dinosaurs in South America, which was previously much poorer than in North America and Europe.
In its original description, Powellvenator was classified within Coelophysoidea as the sister taxon to Coelophysidae, making the parent group of Powellvenator Coelophysidae.
Powellvenator lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately between 221 and 206 million years ago, in what is now South America.
